ranked_variants.title: GC heap/malloc limits and jemalloc THP via environment in start.sh
ranked_variants.spec:
File: submissions/ruby-async-cicloid/start.sh. Before the final `exec bundle exec ruby ...` add:

export RUBY_GC_HEAP_FREE_SLOTS_GOAL_RATIO=0.6 RUBY_GC_HEAP_FREE_SLOTS_MAX_RATIO=0.9 RUBY_GC_HEAP_FREE_SLOTS_MIN_RATIO=0.4 \
       RUBY_GC_MALLOC_LIMIT=134217728 RUBY_GC_MALLOC_LIMIT_MAX=268435456 \
       RUBY_GC_OLDMALLOC_LIMIT=134217728 RUBY_GC_OLDMALLOC_LIMIT_MAX=536870912 \
       RUBY_GC_HEAP_OLDOBJECT_LIMIT_FACTOR=4.0
export MALLOC_CONF="thp:always,metadata_thp:always,background_thread:false"

No RUBY_GC_HEAP_INIT_SLOTS (Process.warmup + the warm-up requests already size and compact the heap). jemalloc is libjemalloc2 5.3.0 linked into /opt/ruby/bin/ruby (verify with ldd); the MALLOC_CONF string must not print 'Invalid conf' at startup. Do not change dirty/muzzy decay (measured neutral, +50 MB RSS).

Measurement plan: build the variant with both groups; if the paired 20k result is flat or negative, build a second image with only the RUBY_GC_* group (THP depends on /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled on the Docker VM; if it reads 'never' the MALLOC_CONF part is a no-op locally and must be re-tested on the x86_64 target). Record RSS (server_peak_mem_mb) - expected +20-60 MB, must stay far below the 2 GB limit - and GC counts (add a one-off `GC.stat(:minor_gc_count)`/`:major_gc_count` stderr line at SIGTERM or every 10 s while measuring). Prior micro: GCs per 128k requests 53 -> 25; with 20k idle connections resident 50 -> 13 GCs and us/req 28.8 -> 25.0 (noisy core). Verify: test/test.sh 42/42; health within 60 s unchanged.
ranked_variants.why_ranked_here: Pure environment change with no code risk; GC is 2.8% of the profile and the GC-count halving is reproducible, but the end-to-end effect is inside harness noise locally and THP cannot be validated on this VM, so it sits below the code changes.

rules.problems: No rule violation found. The change touches only process environment in start.sh: no caching, JWT, durability, response-byte, build-from-source or kernel-parameter surface is affected, and rule 11 names GC and allocator settings as fair game (jemalloc thp:always only issues madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE) on its own mappings; nothing under /sys is written). Verified in tdsc-cicloid:base: libjemalloc.so.2 5.3.0-2build1 is linked (ldd); the MALLOC_CONF string is fully recognised (confirm_conf:true echoes 'Set conf value' for thp, metadata_thp, background_thread, no 'Invalid conf'); all eight RUBY_GC_* values parse in range under `ruby -w` and GC.stat shows malloc_increase_bytes_limit = oldmalloc_increase_bytes_limit = 134217728; without -w stderr stays silent. Wrong assumptions / risks (not violations): (1) The Docker VM's THP mode is `[always]` with defrag `[madvise]` (6.12.76-linuxkit), not 'never': the local baseline already gets THP on all anonymous memory, so the MALLOC_CONF group is close to a no-op locally for the opposite reason the spec gives, and only the x86_64 target (Ubuntu default enabled=madvise) can show its effect. (2) defrag=madvise applies on both the VM and Ubuntu's default, so jemalloc's MADV_HUGEPAGE regions take synchronous compaction on fault; with 2 GB and no swap this is a p99/event-loop-delay stall risk, and THP's 2 MB granularity plus FREE_SLOTS_GOAL 0.6 (heap ~2.5x live instead of ~1.67x) and 128 MB malloc limits all push RSS up; rule 8 makes OOM a loss, so the target run needs an RSS and p99 abort criterion. (3) The measurement plan's 'stderr line at SIGTERM' cannot work locally: local-bench/run.sh tears the server down with `docker rm -f` (SIGKILL), and in test/run.sh (`kill $PID; wait $PID`) a TERM trap that prints without exiting would hang the test runner. (4) Ruby parses the ratios in fixed order MIN, MAX (lower bound MIN), GOAL (bounds MIN..MAX) regardless of shell order and silently ignores an out-of-range value unless -w is on; 0.4 < 0.6 < 0.9 is valid, but any later retune must keep that ordering. (5) background_thread:false is already jemalloc's default; harmless but redundant.
rules.spec_fixes: 1. Replace the THP caveat with: '/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled reads [always] (defrag [madvise]) on the Docker VM, so the baseline already has THP on all anonymous memory and the MALLOC_CONF group is expected to be flat locally; its gain can only be measured on the x86_64 target (Ubuntu 24.04 default enabled=madvise). The RUBY_GC_* group is the only part a local paired run can judge.' 2. GC-count instrumentation: do not use a SIGTERM trap or at_exit (local harness SIGKILLs via docker rm -f; test/run.sh does kill+wait and a non-exiting TERM trap would hang it). Instead add a temporary reactor task in server.rb that every 10 s writes `GC.stat(:minor_gc_count)`, `GC.stat(:major_gc_count)` and `GC.stat(:heap_live_slots)` to stderr (run.sh prints `docker logs --tail 5`, and `docker logs tdsc-srv-<id>` has the full series), and remove it before the submission copy. 3. Add abort criteria for the target run: drop the MALLOC_CONF group if server_peak_mem_mb exceeds baseline by more than ~150 MB at the scoring user count or if p99 / event_loop_delay_ms widen versus the paired baseline (THP direct-compaction stalls under defrag=madvise); drop the RUBY_GC_* group if RSS growth is not matched by a GC-count reduction. 4. Note in the spec that the three FREE_SLOTS ratios must satisfy MIN < GOAL < MAX (Ruby validates MAX against MIN and GOAL against both, and silently ignores violations unless run with -w); verify any retune with `ruby -w -e ''` under the same env before benchmarking. 5. Optionally drop `background_thread:false` (already the default) to keep the string minimal; keep `thp:always,metadata_thp:always`. 6. Keep the exports in start.sh after `export PATH=...` and before `exec bundle exec ruby ...` as written; no Gemfile/Gemfile.lock/install.sh change, so only the app layer rebuilds.

tech.problems:
No API misconception: /opt/ruby/bin/ruby has NEEDED libjemalloc.so.2 (libjemalloc2 5.3.0-2build1); MALLOC_CONF="thp:always,metadata_thp:always,background_thread:false" parses cleanly (a bogus key does print "<jemalloc>: Invalid conf pair", so the startup check is meaningful) and stats_print shows opt.thp "always", opt.metadata_thp "always"; Ruby 4.0.7 `-w` echoes all eight RUBY_GC_* values as accepted and in-bounds (MIN 0.4 < GOAL 0.6 < MAX 0.9), GC.stat reports malloc_increase_bytes_limit=134217728; env passes through `bundle exec`; no code or bytes change (test.sh not run here, the plan keeps it). background_thread:false is already jemalloc's default (no-op).

Wrong assumptions, demonstrated:
1. THP contingency is wrong-shaped. The Docker VM reads /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled = "[always] madvise never" (hugepages-2048kB = inherit), not "never". jemalloc 5.3's pages_set_thp_state() returns early when the system mode equals opt.thp, so thp:always never madvises locally; and /proc/buddyinfo shows 0 free order-9 blocks in the Normal zone (MemFree 1.1 GB, fragmented), so the kernel hands out no huge pages anyway: a Ruby process allocating 64 MiB + 16 MB of heap shows AnonHugePages 0 kB (default) / 4096 kB (thp:always). The MALLOC_CONF half is a double no-op locally and cannot be validated or refuted here. On the x86 droplet (Ubuntu 24.04 default: enabled=madvise, defrag=madvise) it would newly madvise only jemalloc extents (malloc'd strings, SQLite's 64 MiB page cache, libsodium), not Ruby's GC heap pages, which Ruby mmaps itself (nm: mmap/mmap64/madvise imports; 222 GC pages across 53 anon VMAs) and never madvises, so the object heap that marking/sweeping walks gets nothing; defrag=madvise also means synchronous compaction on faults in madvised regions (latency risk of unknown size). Sign on the target is unknown.
2. RSS expectation is off by 2-6x. Real server (tdsc-cicloid:base, fresh seed DB, 20k idle keep-alive connections, load-test mix, 173,605 requests in ~21 s, server CPU from /proc/1/stat in the shared pid namespace): VmHWM 106 MB base -> 235 MB with the full group (+129 MB), both rounds. Attribution: malloc-limit group alone -> 234 MB; ratio+OLDOBJECT group alone -> 116-117 MB. Cause: RUBY_GC_OLDMALLOC_LIMIT 16->128 MB lets ~128 MB of promoted (old) garbage accumulate between majors. The harness's server_peak_mem_mb (cgroup memory.peak) will show about +130 MB; at the 70-80k churn runs (476-485 MB baseline) expect ~600-650 MB. Still far below 2 GB, so not disqualifying.
3. The malloc-limit sub-group does not do what the spec implies. Minor GCs in this server are heap-slot-triggered: RUBY_GC_MALLOC_LIMIT/_MAX + OLDMALLOC alone left minors at 91-99 (base 96-99) and majors 6 (base 7). The entire minor-GC halving comes from the three FREE_SLOTS ratios + OLDOBJECT_LIMIT_FACTOR (minors 49, majors 5, +10 MB RSS); the full group gives 45/3. The feed response is 5,102 bytes, not a large document, so the 128 MB malloc window is pure old-garbage headroom.
4. No measurable CPU effect, and the plan cannot resolve one. CPU/request: base 64.7/64.9/68.7/66.9 vs full group 65.3/66.7/66.7/70.1 us/req (two interleaved A/Bs, 10k then 20k idle connections): pooled +1.4%, within the ±3% run-to-run spread; the harness's own identical-image base runs at 20k spread 49.3-56.5 us/req (±7%). With a claimed 0.7% gain, the single paired 20k/60 s bench will read "flat or negative" by construction, so the plan's branch on that outcome decides nothing. The spec's prior micro (28.8 -> 25.0 us/req with 20k idle) is not reproduced on the real request path. Max theoretical gain from the profile is ~2.8% (GC) + ~2.3% (sweeping) share halved, i.e. inside noise.

Exact-bytes risk: none (environment only).
tech.spec_fixes:
1. Split the GC group and drop the malloc limits: image A = RUBY_GC_HEAP_FREE_SLOTS_MIN_RATIO=0.4 GOAL_RATIO=0.6 MAX_RATIO=0.9 RUBY_GC_HEAP_OLDOBJECT_LIMIT_FACTOR=4.0 only (halves minors 99->49, majors 7->5, +10 MB peak RSS). Image B = A + RUBY_GC_OLDMALLOC_LIMIT at most 33554432-67108864 (each +16 MB of OLDMALLOC_LIMIT is roughly +16 MB peak RSS, majors 7->3 only at 128 MB). Remove RUBY_GC_MALLOC_LIMIT and RUBY_GC_MALLOC_LIMIT_MAX entirely (no minor-GC effect here, +128 MB peak). Remove the sentence "No RUBY_GC_HEAP_INIT_SLOTS ..." rationale is fine but note Process.warmup frees empty pages, so the first few GCs under load regrow the heap to the 0.4/0.6 ratios.
2. MALLOC_CONF: keep "thp:always,metadata_thp:always" as an x86_64-only experiment with its own paired run on the droplet (local VM: THP mode is "always" and has no free 2 MB blocks, so jemalloc never madvises and AnonHugePages stays ~0 regardless); drop background_thread:false (already default). Rewrite the contingency: it is a local no-op whenever enabled reads "always" OR "never"; only "madvise" makes it active. Record /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/{enabled,defrag} and /proc/buddyinfo on the target, and watch p99 (defrag=madvise causes synchronous compaction on madvised faults).
3. Correct the RSS expectation to +130 MB peak for the original full group (+10 MB for image A); keep the "far below 2 GB" gate, expect ~600-650 MB at 70-80k churn.
4. Acceptance evidence: make the GC.stat stderr line the primary evidence (RUBYOPT=-r<file> with a 10 s thread + at_exit works unchanged with `bundle exec` and `docker kill -s TERM`; expect minors roughly halved and majors 7->3-5 per ~170k requests). Accept a CPU/request delta only from >=3 interleaved base/variant pairs whose mean delta exceeds the pair spread; a single paired 20k run cannot resolve 0.7%. Reusable harness: <scratchpad>/ab2.sh (takes a bench-core lock like bench.sh; driver.rb, gcstat.rb beside it).
5. Lower expected_gain_pct to ~0-0.5 for the GC-only image (unmeasurable locally); keep confidence "low"; regime "both" is fine (old-garbage headroom matters most in the churn regime, which is where the OLDMALLOC cost shows).

ranked_variants.title: SQLite pages from the page cache instead of the 1 GiB mmap (PRAGMA mmap_size=0), A/B two cache sizes
ranked_variants.spec:
File: submissions/ruby-async-cicloid/app.rb, Store#initialize pragma block. Primary build: change `PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824` to `PRAGMA mmap_size=0`, keep `PRAGMA cache_size=-65536`. Secondary build (only if the primary is flat or better): additionally `PRAGMA cache_size=-262144` (256 MiB: holds the whole 238 MB seed so like inserts never pread a cold page). All other pragmas (locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE, journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, wal_autocheckpoint=0, temp_store=MEMORY) unchanged. Do not change sqlite_train.c in this variant (keeps it rb-layer; v12 mirrors whichever setting wins into the trainer).

Why it might win: with mmap, clean pages are not retained in the pcache, so each access does walFindFrame -> unixFetch -> pagerAcquireMapPage -> btreeInitPage (re-parsing the page header and cell pointer array); with the pcache the hot pages stay parsed (MemPage.isInit) across statements. Why it might lose: first touch becomes a 4 KiB pread instead of a page fault, and after a like-heavy phase one proposer measured mmap=0 3% slower on the feed. Two proposers measured FEED -4..-9% and POST -5..-8% in micro A/Bs; this is exactly the kind of thing only a paired full bench decides.

Edge cases: RSS grows as the pcache fills (+~70 MB at 64 MiB, up to +240 MB at 256 MiB; limit 2 GB); the existing warm-up touches the feed path so health within 60 s is unaffected; query results identical. Verify: test/test.sh 42/42; paired 20k and 60k runs for each build, report us_per_req and server_peak_mem_mb; keep whichever of {mmap 1 GiB, mmap 0/64 MiB, mmap 0/256 MiB} wins, both directions are acceptable outcomes.
ranked_variants.why_ranked_here: Two lenses independently measured the same direction in micro A/Bs but with counter-evidence after write-heavy phases; a one-line pragma A/B whose answer also decides what v12's trainer should mirror.

rules.problems: No concrete violation found. The variant changes only two per-connection pragmas in Store#initialize (<repo>/submissions/ruby-async-cicloid/app.rb lines 47-48). Rule 5 explicitly permits SQLite's page cache and mmap, so a larger pcache (even one that holds the whole 238 MB seed) is "the database", not a cross-request cache; JWT verification and all SQL text are untouched. Rule 6 is unaffected: journal_mode=WAL and synchronous=NORMAL stay, and SQLite never writes through the mmap, so the durability path is byte-for-byte the same. No kernel tuning, no build/toolchain change (install.sh, build.sh, sqlite_train.c untouched), health/warm-up path unchanged. No response-byte risk: no SQL, key order or formatting changes, and test/test.sh only inspects HTTP status/body, so 42/42 is expected. Memory: the 256 MiB pcache is anonymous heap (not kernel-reclaimable like file-backed mmap pages), but 362 MB peak + 256 MiB + kernel page cache of the 238 MB file is still far below the 2 GB / no-swap limit (rule 8). Minor accuracy note on the proposal's framing, not a rules problem: sqlite_train.c sets neither mmap_size nor cache_size and install.sh defines neither SQLITE_DEFAULT_MMAP_SIZE nor SQLITE_DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE, so the PGO profile was already trained on the non-mmap pcache path (mmap_size=0, cache_size=-2000); the primary build moves the server toward the trainer, and some of any measured gain may be PGO alignment rather than the MemPage.isInit reuse argument.
rules.spec_fixes: 1) Correct the v12 hand-off wording: the trainer currently matches mmap_size=0 (SQLite default; no -DSQLITE_DEFAULT_MMAP_SIZE in install.sh), so if mmap=0 wins, v12 needs no mmap change in sqlite_train.c (optionally mirror cache_size); if mmap=1 GiB wins, v12 should add `PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824` to the trainer's pragma string. 2) Whichever build is kept, update the pragma sentence in the submission README.md (line 66: "1 GiB `mmap_size`; 64 MiB page cache") so the documented design matches the code. 3) Keep both pragmas after `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` and before the prepares, as now; they are per-connection and the single connection is never reopened, so no re-application is needed. 4) In the bench report, record server_peak_mem_mb for both builds and note that pcache memory is anonymous (counts fully against the 2 GB, no-swap box) whereas mmap pages were file-backed and reclaimable; the 256 MiB build must stay comfortably under 2 GB at the 60k run. 5) Since the primary build aligns with the existing PGO profile, treat a gain as real for the submission (PGO is part of the build) but do not attribute it solely to pcache mechanics when deciding what v12 mirrors.

tech.problems:
Premise checked and not refuted; two spec errors and one noise caveat found.

1. APIs: Extralite::Database#execute("PRAGMA mmap_size=0") in extralite 3.1.3 steps the statement and takes effect (verified in the image: PRAGMA mmap_size reads back 0, cache_size -262144 reads back). Note `execute` returns the change count, so reading a pragma back needs `query_single_splat` (`query_single_value` does not exist in 3.1.3). extralite's ext has no sqlite3_config/mmap override; the static SQLite reports DEFAULT_MMAP_SIZE=0, MAX_MMAP_SIZE=0x7fff0000, so mmap_size=0 fully disables mapping.

2. Mechanism confirmed in the 3.54 amalgamation: pagerAcquireMapPage does memset(p->pExtra,0,8) (clears MemPage.isInit) and getAndInitPage re-runs btreeInitPage when isInit==0, so every mmap acquisition re-parses the page; getPageMMap also calls sqlite3WalFindFrame per acquisition, which a pcache hit skips. The pcache is not reset between transactions here (single EXCLUSIVE connection): over 18k mixed iterations mmap=0 added only +4.9k preads (cold sqlite_autoindex_likes_1 leaves for random-user likes), not the ~2.7M a reset would cause.

3. Hot path is hot: local stackprof puts Extralite::Query#next at 36.6% of CPU samples (Store#feed 34.9% inclusive); the C harness counted ~150 page acquisitions per feed (9.57M pcache fetches / ~61k feeds).

4. Measurements (real seed, server pragmas/statements, generator mix feed -> post-from-feed -> 15% like / 2% create each in own txn, PASSIVE checkpoint per 1000 iterations, 3 interleaved rounds, CPU-time, minimums). C against the image's PGO libsqlite3.a: feed pristine 31.7 us (mmap 1 GiB) vs 29.0 / 29.2 us (mmap 0, 64 / 256 MiB); feed in mix 26.0 vs 22.6 / 22.9; feed after writes 22.5 vs 21.0 / 21.4; post 1.5 vs 1.3 / 1.4; like 36.3 vs 37.0 / 36.9 (equal). Ruby+extralite+YJIT in the image: mix feed 26.7 vs 23.4 / 23.0 us, post 1.8 vs 1.5 / 1.5, like 43.6 vs 43.8 / 43.1, mix CPU 0.89 s vs 0.80 / 0.80 s. So pcache is 5-12% cheaper on feed/post SQLite CPU and flat on writes; the "3% slower after a like-heavy phase" counter-evidence did not reproduce (after 3k likes + 400 creates + checkpoints the pcache feed was still faster). Caveat: single runs on this host swing 2x when other agents' benches run (three slots were busy during my Ruby rounds; one round came out 2x on every metric at once), so the full bench must be paired (pair.sh) and repeated with sides swapped; a 1-3% total effect is inside the harness's unpaired noise (base image spans 49-110 us/req across results/*.jsonl).

5. The secondary build is a no-op: B (64 MiB) and C (256 MiB) had identical sqlite3_db_status counters (9,568,200 hits / 6,225 misses, 32 MB cache used). The generator takes post ids from the feed, so the working set is ~32 MB (hot feed pages + random-user leaves of sqlite_autoindex_likes_1, 31 MB total, and posts_user_id_idx, 5.5 MB; tokens cover 20k users) and a 64 MiB cache never evicts. The rationale "256 MiB holds the seed so like inserts never pread a cold page" is wrong: a first touch is a pread at any cache size; only eviction would make size matter and there is none.

6. Memory estimate is an overestimate: VmHWM dropped with mmap=0 (Ruby 110 -> 74 MB, C 71 -> 35 MB) because mapped file pages count in RSS while the pcache holds only the working set; over 5 minutes it grows to roughly the working set (~40-45 MB), not +70/+240 MB. No 2 GB risk either way.

7. Expected size of the win: ~3 us per feed and ~0.3 us per post of SQLite CPU; feed and post are each ~46% of requests, so roughly -1.5 us per request on average, i.e. ~1.5-3% of the ~50-65 us/req the local harness currently reports for base (less on the x86 droplet where SQLite is ~15% of samples). "0.7%, low confidence" is the right order.

8. Side finding relevant to v12: sqlite_train.c never sets mmap_size, so the PGO profile was already collected on the pcache path (SQLite default mmap 0, cache 2 MB). If mmap=0 wins there is nothing for the trainer to mirror; if mmap 1 GiB wins, the trainer is the one out of sync.
tech.spec_fixes:
- Drop the secondary build (cache_size=-262144): measured identical pcache hit/miss counts and cache usage (32 MB) at 64 and 256 MiB; the working set is ~32-45 MB because post ids come from the feed. Keep cache_size=-65536. If the slot is spent anyway, treat it only as a memory sanity check, not as a candidate.
- Verification must be paired: run pair.sh base vs variant at 20k (and 60k) at least twice with sides swapped; discard a run where every metric moves together by 2x (host interference). Compare us_per_req deltas, not absolutes; expect about -1.5 us/req (1.5-3% locally), below the unpaired noise floor.
- Correct the memory note: mmap=0 lowers RSS in practice (file-backed mapped pages leave RSS, pcache holds only the working set); +70/+240 MB are unreachable upper bounds in this workload.
- Read pragmas back with query_single_splat (not execute, which returns the change count; query_single_value does not exist in extralite 3.1.3).
- v12 note: sqlite_train.c already trains with mmap_size=0 (SQLite default in this build), so mirroring is only needed if mmap 1 GiB is kept.
- Keep expected_gain_pct at ~0.7-1.5 with low confidence; writes (like/create) are flat within noise in both harnesses, so no regression is expected on the POST path.

ranked_variants.title: Churn regime: shed newcomers at accept (never registered in epoll) and send the closing response with MSG_MORE so the FIN rides on it
ranked_variants.spec:
File: submissions/ruby-async-cicloid/http.rb. Only changes behaviour when `@open > @budget` (budget = soft nofile - 256), i.e. at the 80k point; at 20k it must be a no-op.

1. New state `SHED = 3`. In `accept_loop` (93-110), after `@open += 1; fd = socket.fileno; @sockets[fd] = socket`:
   if @open > @budget && @shed_in_flight < 2048
     @state[fd] = SHED; @shed_in_flight += 1
     socket.timeout = 10                       # Async's io_read honours IO#timeout: a client that never sends raises IO::TimeoutError -> rescue IOError -> disconnect
     @ready.push(fd); add_worker if @waiting < @ready.size && @workers < MAX_WORKERS
   else
     @state[fd] = IDLE; Epoll.control(@epfd, Epoll::CTL_ADD, fd, @event)
   end
   (initialise `@shed_in_flight = 0` in `run`; decrement it in `disconnect` when the state being cleared is SHED/was shed - keep a per-fd flag or check `@state[fd] == SHED` before clearing.)

2. `service` (164-196): `shed = @state[fd] == SHED` before the outer loop; change `@state[fd] = BUSY` to `@state[fd] = BUSY unless shed`. The first read is today's `Fiber.scheduler.io_read(socket, io_buffer, 1, 0)`, which on a fresh socket simply completes when the request bytes arrive (one RTT after accept) - no epoll registration or readiness pass needed. If the request is incomplete (inner loop broke on :wait_readable with `buffer` non-nil and `drain` returned a partial `rest`): for a shed fd do NOT go IDLE (it is not in epoll, nobody would wake it): instead `@partial[fd] = rest; socket.wait_readable; next` (scheduler wait with the 10 s timeout) and re-enter the outer loop. Pass `shed` to drain: `drain(socket, buffer, shed)`.

3. `drain` (266): replace `close ||= @open > @budget` with `close ||= shed || @open > @budget + 192`. Kept connections now stay keep-alive while over budget unless the population exceeds budget + 192 (= soft - 64, still below EMFILE), in which case the old 'close any served connection' rule resumes as the hard ceiling. A shed connection is therefore always answered with `Connection: close` and closed by `disconnect` (drain returns nil), so it never enters epoll.

4. FIN on the last segment: `respond(socket, heads, status, document)` passes `heads.equal?(CLOSE)` to write: `def write(socket, data, last = false)`; when `last`: `offset = 0; while offset < data.bytesize; n = socket.send(offset.zero? ? data : data.byteslice(offset, data.bytesize - offset), Socket::MSG_MORE); offset += n; end` (send is a direct sendto, verified by strace; BasicSocket#send retries through the scheduler on EAGAIN); otherwise `socket.write(data)` as today. `reject` uses CLOSE so error responses get it too. With MSG_MORE the kernel holds the last partial segment and merges it with the FIN from close (measured 10 -> 8 TCP segments per churned connection); full-MSS segments still leave immediately.

Edge cases: `@open`, `@sockets`, `@state`, `@partial` and the shed counter must be cleaned in `disconnect` exactly as today; a shed fd can never receive an epoll event (not registered) so AGAIN never applies to it; HTTP/1.0 and `Connection: close` request paths unchanged; the `rescue Errno::EMFILE ... sleep 0.01` path unchanged.

Verify: test/test.sh 42/42; a hand test that opens a socket, waits 11 s without sending, and sees it closed; 20k paired run must be neutral (nothing is shed); 80k paired runs (both base and variant in the same slot) reporting pass/fail, p95/p99, connects and retired_connections; capture `nstat -az TcpExtListenOverflows TcpExtListenDrops TcpRetransSegs` (or /proc/net/netstat deltas) inside tdsc-srv-<id> before/after the 80k hold for both runs - the baseline's p95 1059 ms / p99 1312 ms at 57% CPU is a SYN-RTO-shaped tail; if overflows are non-zero in the variant too, report it: the next churn step is fd headroom at accept (a larger budget margin), not CPU. Prior evidence: per churned request accept 6 us + epoll_ctl ADD 3.1-3.6 us + epoll event + extra reactor pass + close 4 us; fsharp-kestrel measured the FIN merge at -4.6% CPU/req at 160k users (~1.4% scaled to cicloid's ~18% churned share at 80k).
ranked_variants.why_ranked_here: The only slot whose success criterion is making 80k pass / shrinking p95-p99 rather than us/req; it bundles the three churn mechanisms that stay inside the rules (no load-test-shaped policy) and is a no-op at 20k so it cannot hurt the keep-alive number. Ranked low because the 80k failure locally looks accept-queue/latency bound, which this may or may not fix, and it conflicts with v02/v03/v05/v06/v11 in http.rb.

rules.problems:
No rule violation found. Checked against README "Rules" and SPEC.md with the code at submissions/ruby-async-cicloid/http.rb:
- Caching / JWT / durability: untouched (variant is http.rb only; app.rb group commit and per-request HMAC unchanged; `@partial` is per-connection request bytes, pre-existing).
- Exact bytes / key order: response bytes are identical; only TCP segmentation of `Connection: close` responses changes. test/test.sh never receives a CLOSE response: curl sends well-formed HTTP/1.1 serially, every 400 in the suite is an app-level KEEP response (`invalid post id`, `malformed JSON body`, ...), `reject` (431/400/411/413) is never reached, and @open is ~1 so the shed branch is dead at test time.
- Build from source / kernel tuning: no Gemfile change; MSG_MORE is a per-call send(2) flag and IO#timeout is process-internal; no sysctl. Not load-test shaped: shedding keys off the same descriptor-pressure signal the baseline already uses (`@open` vs rlimit); behaviour at <= budget is identical to baseline.
Runtime claims verified inside tdsc-cicloid:base with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` (URing selector; note a plain `docker run` silently falls back to EPoll because Docker's default seccomp blocks io_uring): Socket::MSG_MORE=32768; IO::TimeoutError < IOError; accept_nonblock sockets are O_NONBLOCK; Async 2.46 `Scheduler#io_read`/`io_write`/`io_wait` arm a timer from `io.timeout` and `fiber.raise(IO::TimeoutError)` (vendor/bundle/ruby/4.0.0/gems/async-2.46.0/lib/async/scheduler.rb:311-385) -- measured 1.01 s for `Fiber.scheduler.io_read`, 1.0 s for `wait_readable`; `send(data, MSG_MORE)` then `close` delivered all bytes then EOF; a stalled `send` retried through the scheduler on EAGAIN and raised IO::TimeoutError at io.timeout when the peer never read.
Concrete risks (test/robustness, not rules):
1. test.sh WILL fail if `drain` is changed to `def drain(socket, buffer, shed)` with no default: `warm` (http.rb:83) calls `drain(near, request.b)` before `run`, so the server raises ArgumentError at boot and never listens (run.sh reports "server died").
2. Headroom: the hard ceiling `@budget + 192` = soft-64 leaves ~44-54 fds for newcomers once the process's ~10-20 fixed fds (stdio, listener, epfd, io_uring ring+eventfd, SQLite db+WAL, Ruby signal pipe) are counted, versus 256 today. The baseline already runs into EMFILE at 70k-80k here (loadgen peak_connections 65,687-66,042 > 65,535 in base70k/base75k/base80k.jsonl), and the 80k tail is accept-queue/SYN-RTO shaped per the spec's own diagnosis; narrowing headroom makes `EMFILE -> sleep 0.01 -> backlog overflow` more likely, which is the exact failure mode the variant targets.
3. Close-with-unread-data: with MSG_MORE the response tail sits in the send queue until close(2); if the peer has pipelined bytes the server has not read at that instant, Linux sends RST and discards the unsent tail (truncated response). The baseline's window is near zero because NODELAY pushed the data already. curl, k6/Go net/http and connection_load.c never pipeline, so no test or score impact, but it is a behavioural regression for pipelining clients.
4. `socket.timeout = 10` also bounds the response write of a shed socket (a client that does not drain a 5 KB feed within 10 s is dropped); it is rescued by the existing `rescue IOError` -> `disconnect`, which must decrement the shed counter (spec already says to check `@state[fd] == SHED` before clearing).
5. The "wait 11 s without sending, see it closed" hand test is only reachable when `@open > @budget`, i.e. after ~65.3k connections; it needs a run with a small hard nofile (start.sh raises soft to hard, so `--ulimit nofile=1024:1024` -> budget 921).
rules.spec_fixes:
1. Give `drain` a default: `def drain(socket, buffer, shed = false)` (or update `warm` to pass false). Mandatory, otherwise the server does not boot and test.sh fails.
2. Preserve the 256-descriptor headroom: shed above `@budget - 192` and keep the hard ceiling at `@budget` (`close ||= shed || @open > @budget`), instead of raising the ceiling to `@budget + 192`. Same 192-wide band between "shed newcomers" and "close any served connection", no reduction in EMFILE margin. If the +192 ceiling is kept, count the process's fixed descriptors once at `run` (e.g. `Dir.children("/proc/self/fd").size`) and derive the margin from it rather than assuming 64 is enough.
3. Initialise `@shed_in_flight = 0` in `initialize` (next to `@open = 0`) rather than in `run`, so `disconnect`/`warm` can never see nil.
4. State explicitly that `dispatch`'s `case @state[fd]` keeps no `else` branch: a stale epoll event carrying a reused fd number (a closed fd whose epoll registration lingers while an in-flight io_uring op holds the file) must be ignored when that fd is now SHED.
5. In `accept_loop`, set `socket.timeout = 10` and `@state[fd] = SHED` before `@ready.push(fd)` (keep the order as written).
6. Optional, only if pipelining clients matter: `socket.shutdown(Socket::SHUT_WR)` before `close` in the shed/close path flushes the corked tail with the FIN before any RST; it costs one extra syscall per churned connection, so measure before adopting.
7. Verification protocol: run the probe/hand test and the 80k runs with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` (bench.sh/run.sh already do); for the 11 s idle hand test use `--ulimit nofile=1024:1024` so `@budget` is reachable. Also capture `/proc/self/fd` count at steady state in both runs alongside the nstat deltas, so EMFILE sleeps can be attributed.
8. Update the submission README's "Direct instead of Nginx" paragraph to describe the shed-at-accept policy, the 10 s first-request timeout on shed connections and the MSG_MORE close path (rule: README documents the optimizations).

tech.problems:
1. WRONG PREMISE (demonstrated): the baseline does NOT fail at 80k locally, and there is no SYN-RTO/accept-queue tail. Two fresh 80k baseline runs (tdsc-cicloid:base, --seconds 120 --ramp 30), run concurrently on separate slots with /proc/net/netstat+snmp snapshotted every 5 s inside tdsc-srv-<id>: procs=1 -> pass, p95 13.7 ms, p99 33.2 ms, 36.3% CPU, 42.8 us/req, connects 261,919, retired 196,675 (local-bench/results/skep80k-p1.jsonl); procs=2 -> pass, p95 22.4 ms, p99 114 ms, 37.4% CPU, 44.0 us/req, connects 262,153, retired 196,880 (local-bench/results/skep80k-p2.jsonl). Netstat totals over both holds: ListenOverflows=0, ListenDrops=0, TCPSynRetrans=0, RetransSegs=0, TCPTimeouts=0, TCPAbortOnClose=0, OutRsts=0, PassiveOpens=258.6k each (snapshots + deltas: <scratchpad>/net-skep80k-p1/, <scratchpad>/net-skep80k-p2/, analyser <scratchpad>/netdelta.py). The recorded base80k failure (p95 1059 ms, 57.5% CPU, 69 us/req, results/base80k.jsonl, 23:07) was taken at the same minute as base100k and is a host-contention artefact, not a server regime. Consequence: the variant's success criterion 'make 80k pass / shrink p95-p99' has no target; the only measurable claim left is us_per_req (and connects/retired) in the churn regime. Also note the loadgen's p95/p99 exclude connect time (connection_load.c:5, request_begin set after connect completes), so a pure SYN retransmit could never show in p95/p99 anyway; only a dropped final-ACK on listen overflow (tcp_abort_on_overflow=0) could, and overflows are zero.
2. FIN-merge overclaim: measured in the image (Async + URing selector, seccomp=unconfined like the bench; <scratchpad>/skep/fin_test.rb) write+close vs send(MSG_MORE)+close for a 3 KB body: OutSegs per connection 10.0 -> 9.0 (both directions, same netns), TCPPureAcks unchanged at 4.0, 0 RSTs, responses byte-exact. So one server segment saved per churned connection, not two ('10 -> 8' comes from another agent's client pattern). For a 100 KB body (over the loopback MSS) there is no saving at all (13.0 vs 13.1) - irrelevant here since /feed is 3,385 bytes and /posts/:id 195 bytes (curl against the live server), but do not expect it to generalise.
3. The live gain attribution is probably wrong: at 80k the baseline churns 25.4% of requests (258.6k passive opens / 1.016M requests) because 'close every served connection while @open > budget' over-closes; the minimum is the excess users' share, (80000-65279)/80000 = 18.4%. Step 3 of the spec (incumbents stay keep-alive up to budget+192) removes that over-closing, i.e. ~600 fewer connects/s at ~40-50 us of server CPU each (other agent's per-connection costing: write_close 50.6 us/conn, msgmore_close 41.0 us/conn) - that policy change, not the epoll skip or the FIN merge, is likely the largest CPU effect and must be separated in the report (compare connects/retired_connections between base and variant).
4. API facts verified (no misconceptions found): Ruby 4.0.7 has RUBY_FIBER_SCHEDULER_VERSION 3, so io-event 1.22.1 takes the v3 io_read path where Fiber.scheduler.io_read(socket, buf, 1, 0) means length=1 minimum, offset=0, and ALWAYS submits an SQE and transfers (no optimistic read in v3), so a shed read still costs one reactor pass; the saving is exactly epoll_ctl ADD + the epoll event + one extra pass, as the spec says. async 2.46 Scheduler#io_read and #io_wait arm @timers.after(io.timeout) and fiber.raise(IO::TimeoutError) (scheduler.rb:311-360); io-event's uring io_read cancels via rb_ensure/cancel_and_wait. Behavioural test (<scratchpad>/skep/api_test.rb, URing selector): io_read on a silent client raised IO::TimeoutError after 1.0 s and is caught by rescue IOError; close afterwards fine, reactor alive; socket.wait_readable (nil timeout) also raised after 1.0 s; late data read and the wait_readable+read_nonblock partial path work; client FIN -> read_nonblock nil. Accepted sockets are non-blocking (nonblock?=true) and inherit TCP_NODELAY; send(data, MSG_MORE) into a full SO_SNDBUF returned a partial count (32768), then yielded to the reactor on EAGAIN (ticker kept ticking 20/20) and completed - the spec's send loop is correct. Socket::MSG_MORE = 32768. Timer cost per shed read ~0.5-2 us (5.1-5.4 vs 5.9-7.3 us per write+io_read).
5. Error path: close with unread request data sends RST in BOTH modes; the client saw ECONNRESET 20/20 with plain write+close as well as with MSG_MORE (<scratchpad>/skep/unread_close.rb), so reject() using MSG_MORE is not a regression. test/test.sh has no 411/413/431/HTTP/1.0 cases, so no exact-bytes exposure there.
6. Common path at 20k: the added work is one integer compare in accept_loop, two compares in service/drain and an equal? in respond - unmeasurable; confirmed no-op by construction. One compile-time break: warm() calls drain(near, request.b) with two args; the new shed parameter needs a default or warm must pass false, or the server fails at startup.
7. Tooling: nstat/ss/strace/tcpdump are NOT in the image; read /proc/net/netstat and /proc/net/snmp instead (the wrapper <scratchpad>/netstat-bench.sh already does it). somaxconn inside the container is 4096 (listen(65535) is capped), still never overflowed at 80k. Plain `docker run` picks the EPoll selector because Docker's default seccomp blocks io_uring; any micro-test must use --security-opt seccomp=unconfined to match the bench (URing).

a) Replace the success criterion: both 80k baselines pass with 0 ListenOverflows/ListenDrops/RetransSegs, so judge the variant on paired 80k us_per_req (baseline 42.8-44.0 us/req at 36-37% CPU, p95 14-22 ms, p99 33-114 ms) plus connects and retired_connections, not on pass/fail or a p95/p99 tail. If a latency target is wanted, first re-measure the baseline's real knee under clean conditions (>=100k; results/base100k.jsonl is from the same contended minute).
b) Report the three mechanisms separately: expect connects/s to drop from ~2,160 to ~1,560 (18.4% of requests) from step 3 alone; attribute CPU to that before crediting the epoll skip or the FIN merge. Consider a sub-variant with step 3 only (close ||= @open > @budget + 192 with shed-at-accept of newcomers but no MSG_MORE) to isolate it.
c) FIN merge: state it as 1 segment of ~10 per churned connection (server data+FIN), only for responses below the MSS; expected CPU effect at 80k is ~0.25 segment per request (~5% of segments), on the order of 1%.
d) Code: give drain a default (def drain(socket, buffer, shed = false)) so warm() keeps working; precompute @hard = @budget + 192 in initialize (budget 65279, hard 65471; the running server holds ~14 non-socket fds - 2 eventpoll, 2 eventfd, 2 pipes, io_uring, 3 db files, stdio - so hard leaves ~50 fds before EMFILE: do not widen the +192 margin); keep MAX_WORKERS in mind since shed fds enter @ready straight from accept_loop and grow the pool (gc.out: minor GC 1.5 ms at 256 fibers, 6.9 ms at 4096) - log @workers at the end of the run.

Keep the hand test (silent socket closed after ~10 s) - the timeout path is verified to work with the URing selector.

ranked_variants.title: Dispatcher re-polls epoll with timeout 0 after a non-empty pass; io_uring POLL_ADD only when nothing was ready
ranked_variants.spec:
Files: submissions/ruby-async-cicloid/epoll.rb and http.rb. (1) epoll.rb `Epoll.ready(epfd, events, max)`: make the method return the number of events, i.e. the `epoll_wait` result (keep the local that holds it and make it the last expression after the `while` loop; return 0 on EINTR as today). (2) http.rb `dispatch` (121-137):

  def dispatch
    poller = IO.for_fd(@epfd, autoclose: false)
    events = Epoll.events(MAX_EVENTS)
    while true
      count = Epoll.ready(@epfd, events, MAX_EVENTS) do |fd|
        # existing body unchanged: IDLE -> BUSY + @ready.push + add_worker rule; BUSY -> AGAIN
      end
      if count.zero?
        poller.wait_readable      # nothing pending: park on the io_uring poll exactly as today
      else
        Fiber.scheduler.yield     # let this pass's workers run, then epoll_wait(0) again without an SQE
      end
    end
  end

Semantics: edge-triggered events are not lost (the epoll fd is simply read again); the IDLE/BUSY/AGAIN state machine is untouched; when load stops the loop parks on wait_readable so there is no busy spin; `Fiber.scheduler.yield` puts the dispatcher at the back of the ready queue so accept_loop and the checkpoint timer still run between passes. Cost model: a dispatch pass today is always io_wait SQE + enter + CQE + two fiber transfers (~3-4 us) then epoll_wait(0); under load events are almost always pending when a pass ends (README: ~5.6 requests per epoll_wait at 40k), so the re-poll saves the round trip on most passes and costs one empty epoll_wait(0) (~0.4 us) plus a yield (~1.2 us) once per burst. Verify: test/test.sh 42/42; strace -c on the server during a 20k hold shows io_uring_enter per request drop while epoll_pwait per request rises slightly; paired 20k bench (effect is small, ~0.3%, so run two pairs and also compare p99).
ranked_variants.why_ranked_here: Cheap, isolated and mechanically sound, but the arithmetic gain is ~0.3% and no one measured it end-to-end; it earns a slot because the two lenses agreed and it stacks with v02/v03 to give the readiness-loop + direct-syscall shape of the fastest entries.

rules.problems:
No rules violation found. The change is confined to the dispatcher loop (epoll.rb Epoll.ready return value, http.rb dispatch): it does not touch app.rb, Store, JWT verification, pragmas, response bytes, Gemfile*, install.sh/build.sh, or anything kernel-side, so rules 5 (no caching), 6 (durability), 7 (no hard-coding), 10 (built from source) and 11 (no tuning) are unaffected, and it stays pure Ruby.

Evidence gathered: (a) applied the spec literally to a referee copy at "<repo>/local-bench/variants/v11ref" (image tdsc-cicloid:v11ref): bench.sh --test prints passed=42 failed=0 (both branches are exercised: count>0 -> yield on every request, count==0 -> wait_readable afterwards). (b) No busy spin: after a 300-request burst the standalone container used 11 ms CPU over 3.1 s idle (includes the 1 s checkpoint timer), ruby in state S. (c) Gem internals support the spec's semantics: async-2.46.0 lib/async/scheduler.rb:199 defines Scheduler#yield -> selector.yield; io-event-1.22.1 selector.c IO_Event_Selector_ready_flush uses a placeholder, so a fiber that yields during a flush is resumed on the NEXT select pass (after timers/accept completions are processed), and uring.c:1680 only blocks in io_uring when no fiber is ready, so the loop parks once the dispatcher calls wait_readable.

One inaccuracy in the spec (not a rules issue, but a robustness regression if implemented literally): "return 0 on EINTR as today" is wrong. Today Epoll.ready has no EINTR branch; epoll_wait returns -1 on EINTR/any error, the while loop does nothing and the method returns nil, after which dispatch goes back to wait_readable. If `ready` is simply made the last expression, -1 reaches `count.zero?` (false) and the dispatcher yields and re-polls. That is harmless for a transient EINTR, but a persistent error (e.g. EBADF, EFAULT) turns into a silent 100% CPU yield/epoll_wait(0) loop instead of today's behaviour where wait_readable raises and the failure is visible.
rules.spec_fixes: 1. In dispatch, branch on `count.positive?` (then `Fiber.scheduler.yield`) and fall through to `poller.wait_readable` for 0 and negative results; or equivalently clamp in Epoll.ready with `ready.negative? ? 0 : ready`. Prefer the dispatch-side `positive?` check so a dead epoll fd still raises out of wait_readable rather than spinning. 2. Reword "return 0 on EINTR as today" to "today the method returns nil and -1 from epoll_wait is never inspected; the new code must not treat a negative result as 'events pending'". 3. `while true` vs `loop do` makes no difference; either is fine. 4. Optional: note in the README that the dispatcher re-polls epoll with timeout 0 after a non-empty pass and parks on wait_readable only when it drains, since the README documents the dispatch design.

tech.problems:
No concrete, demonstrated reason to reject: all APIs exist, the mechanism works as described, 42/42 tests pass, and the common path is not measurably slower. But the gain claim does not survive measurement and several spec statements are off. Evidence (all paths under the repo root "<repo>"; variant built at local-bench/variants/v11-dispatch-repoll, image tdsc-cicloid:v11-dispatch-repoll):

1. APIs verified in the image (ruby 4.0.7, async 2.46.0, io-event 1.22.1). Fiber.scheduler.yield -> Async::Scheduler#yield -> @selector.yield -> IO_Event_Selector_yield (selector.c): pushes the current fiber onto the ready queue and transfers to the loop. Ready queue is FIFO (queue_push at head, ready_flush pops from tail) and ready_flush uses a placeholder so fibers pushed during a flush run on the next select, so the dispatcher re-polls only after the workers unblocked in the same pass have run, and there is no starvation/busy spin. Timers fire in run_once! after each select; accept_loop is woken by its own CQE, not by the dispatcher's yield order (spec wording about accept_loop/timer ordering is mechanically slightly off; conclusion unaffected). URing#io_wait does POLL_ADD with deferred submission, so the merge of POLL_ADD into the next select's flush happens as the spec expects.

2. Cost model overstated 2-3x. Micro-benchmark on core 0 with YJIT (scratchpad micro.rb): FFI epoll_wait(timeout 0) 0.31-0.36 us with 0 ready / 0.47-0.51 us with 1 ready; Fiber.scheduler.yield 0.76-0.99 us; today's inline-completing wait_readable round trip 1.17-1.18 us (spec says 3-4 us). Per-pass delta is about -0.35 us on a hit (ready(1)+yield 1.33-1.35 us vs today's 1.68-1.71 us) and +0.3-0.7 us on a miss (ready(0)+yield 1.07-1.19 us added before the park). At ~1 pass per 5-6 requests the ceiling is ~0.05-0.1 us/req, i.e. <=0.2% of 42-44 us/req, below the harness noise floor (baseline spread across runs 42-56 us/req at 20k).

3. End-to-end: zero within noise and p99 not improved. Paired 20k/60s/ramp-20 (results in local-bench/results/v11sk-p1-{A,B}.jsonl, v11sk-p2-{A,B}.jsonl): pair1 base 44.2 us/req (p95 2.907 ms, p99 107.697 ms) vs variant 44.5 (p95 3.397, p99 248.909); pair2 (order swapped) variant 42.3 (p95 2.543, p99 33.491) vs base 42.5 (p95 1.703, p99 24.551). Net CPU +0.7% / -0.5%; p95 and p99 worse for the variant in both pairs (p99 is dominated by run-to-run noise here, but it certainly did not improve). The spec's "compare p99" criterion would reject the variant on this data.

4. Syscall mechanism confirmed but total syscalls go up. strace -c over 30 s mid-hold windows (~63.4k requests each, images tdsc-cicloid:v11sk-strace, logs in scratchpad v11sk-st-{var,base}.strace): variant io_uring_enter 22139, epoll_pwait 18881, pwrite64 36244, total 88096; base io_uring_enter 27088, epoll_pwait 11366, pwrite64 35677, total 84743. io_uring_enter/req -18%, epoll_pwait/req +66%, total syscalls +4% because every non-empty pass now pays an extra epoll_wait(0) that usually returns 0. us/req under strace identical (64.2 vs 64.4).

5. Code details the spec must get right: Epoll.ready today returns nil (last expression is the while loop), not 0, and raw epoll_wait returns -1 on EINTR, so without a clamp `count.zero?` is false on EINTR and the dispatcher would yield-spin instead of parking. The pre-existing local-bench/variants/v11ref copy returns the raw value and has exactly this bug; v11-dispatch-repoll clamps it. YJIT: the spec's `while true` is the right shape (227.8 ns/iter vs 389.5 ns/iter for `loop do`, scratchpad yjit_loop.rb), even though a once-called method body is never JIT-compiled (no loop OSR).

6. Disclosure: my first micro-benchmark container was pinned to core 1 without a harness slot lock while another agent's tdsc-srv-v03p5-base60k server held that core for several minutes before I killed it; that run finished at 41.4 us/req (p99 17.6 ms), consistent with its siblings, so I believe it was not materially skewed, but treat v03p5-base60k with a note. All my pair/strace runs used the proper slot locks on cores 1-3.
tech.spec_fixes:
1. Epoll.ready: clamp before looping and return the count: `ready = epoll_wait(epfd, events, count, 0); ready = 0 if ready.negative?; ...; ready`. State explicitly that today's method returns nil and the raw syscall returns -1 on EINTR; do not use the v11ref copy as a base.
2. Keep `while true` in dispatch (measured faster than `loop do`); keep the single `Fiber.scheduler.yield` after a non-empty pass and `poller.wait_readable` only when count.zero?.
3. Replace the cost model: inline wait_readable round trip is ~1.2 us, not 3-4 us; epoll_wait(0) miss is ~0.35 us; per-pass delta is about -0.35 us on a hit and +0.3-0.7 us on a miss; theoretical ceiling <=0.2% at 20k.
4. expected_gain: ~0% at 20k (measured +0.7%/-0.5%, within noise); at most ~0.1% at 71k; confidence stays low. Reclassify as a shape/stacking change (fewer io_uring_enter per pass, which only pays off if combined with a variant that removes other enters, e.g. the write/read batching variants) rather than a standalone gain.
5. Verification criterion: drop "compare p99" (p99 noise at 20k is tens to hundreds of ms run-to-run and the variant was worse in both pairs); use "not slower in two swapped pairs within +-1% us/req" plus strace -c showing io_uring_enter/req down ~15-20% and epoll_pwait/req up ~60-70%, and note total syscalls/req rise ~4% by design.
6. Correct the ordering sentence: timers fire in Async::Scheduler#run_once! after each select, and accept_loop is resumed by its own CQE in the same flush; the dispatcher's yield only guarantees it runs after the workers it just unblocked (FIFO ready queue + placeholder), which is the property that matters.

ranked_variants.title: SQLite toolchain: PGO trainer that matches the server (pragmas, FEED text, data scale, id distribution) plus compile-flag trims
ranked_variants.spec:
Files: submissions/ruby-async-cicloid/sqlite_train.c and install.sh (SQLITE_FLAGS at lines 29-31). Toolchain rebuild (install.sh runs the trainer and the PGO build).

A. sqlite_train.c fidelity: (1) pragma string = exactly the server's: `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON; PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824; PRAGMA cache_size=-65536; PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY;` (use mmap_size=0 instead if v09 wins; whichever app.rb ships); (2) FEED text = v01's new text without the aggregate ORDER BY (and LIKE text = v04's VALUES upsert if that ships; otherwise the current INSERT..SELECT); (3) scale the synthetic DB toward the seed: recursive-CTE bounds 5k/50k/200k -> 50000 users / 500000 posts / 2000000 likes with the modulo constants adjusted, keep ANALYZE; (4) choose post ids for POST and LIKE the way the load does, from the 20 newest posts (`max_post_id - seed % 20`, tracking max_post_id after each create) instead of uniform over all posts; (5) keep the 1:1 feed:post, 1/7 like, 1/49 create mix and the checkpoint every 1000 iterations. The `-Werror=missing-profile` gate stays.

B. install.sh SQLITE_FLAGS: `-DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=2` -> `-DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=0` (safe: one reactor thread owns the connection, gvl_release_threshold=-1, the checkpoint is an Async task not a Thread - keep it that way and say so in a comment); remove `-DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA` (extralite 3.1.3 never calls the column_*_name APIs; verified to build and run); add `-DSQLITE_OMIT_DECLTYPE -DSQLITE_OMIT_UTF16 -DSQLITE_OMIT_AUTHORIZATION -DSQLITE_OMIT_TRACE`; add `-DSQLITE_MAX_MMAP_SIZE=0` only if mmap_size=0 ships. Do NOT add OMIT_PROGRESS_CALLBACK (extralite calls sqlite3_progress_handler), OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION (extconf have_func + Database#load_extension) or OMIT_AUTOINIT.

Verify: install.sh completes and the profile gate passes; build time delta reported (larger seeding adds seconds); test/test.sh 42/42; paired 20k bench. Honest expectation: flag trims measured within noise in three interleaved non-PGO builds; the fidelity change is worth something only because PGO is already ~11% on FEED in this toolchain (36 -> 31.9 us) and the current profile trains the pcache path on a 10x smaller DB with uniform ids and the old sorter plan.
ranked_variants.why_ranked_here: Hygiene that keeps the SQLite PGO profile aligned with v01/v04/v09 once they land; low expected gain and a full toolchain rebuild, so last. It should be built after v01/v09 results are known so the trainer mirrors the winning text and pragma.

rules.problems: No rule violation found. Request path, JWT verification, runtime pragmas (WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, DEFAULT_WAL_SYNCHRONOUS=1 kept), response bytes and kernel are untouched; everything still builds from the amalgamation with the -Werror=missing-profile gate; sqlite_train.c is a build-time trainer, not a server extension. Flag trims verified against extralite 3.1.3's C sources in tdsc-cicloid:base: it never references sqlite3_trace*/sqlite3_expanded_sql/sqlite3_sql (Database#trace is a Ruby-proc hook), sqlite3_set_authorizer, sqlite3_column_decltype, sqlite3_column_{database,table,origin}_name, any *16 API, sqlite3_config, sqlite3_threadsafe or sqlite3_initialize; it does call sqlite3_progress_handler and sqlite3_load_extension, so the do-not-omit list is correct. Seed DB is UTF-8 (header byte 59 = 1). THREADSAFE=0 premise holds: extralite maps gvl_release_threshold < 0 to GVL_HOLD (inline call, never rb_thread_call_without_gvl), sqlite3_open_v2 runs under the GVL, the checkpoint is task.async in server.rb, http.rb's Thread::Queue is fiber-only, no Thread.new anywhere. Wrong assumptions in the spec (fidelity, not rules): (1) 'INSERT OR IGNORE' with coprime multipliers collapses to one like per post: measured 50,000 distinct (user,post) pairs from the current 200k CTE, and only 500,000 from the naive 7/13 scaling to 2M, so the stated 2,000,000 likes would not materialise. (2) 'exactly the server's pragma string' as quoted puts journal_mode=WAL before locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE; app.rb lines 42-49 set locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE first (immaterial for the heap WAL-index, since the WAL opens at the first transaction after the switch, but not literal). (3) The 10x larger seeding under the instrumented build adds 10x more profile counts for bulk-append/FK-check/ANALYZE paths the server never runs, in btree/pager functions shared with the request path, while the workload loop stays at 40k iterations; the profile drifts toward seeding, against the variant's purpose. (4) /opt/sqlite/VERSION marker '3540000-pgo' is unchanged by the flag edits, so any box or tree with an existing /opt/sqlite skips the rebuild, and vendor/bundle keeps an extralite_ext.so linked against the old static lib (bundle install does not rebuild it); harmless on the clean droplet/CI and in the Docker harness (install.sh layer change invalidates build.sh), but a trap for local reruns.
rules.spec_fixes: A3: generate 2,000,000 distinct likes with a bucketed formula instead of coprime multipliers, e.g. post_id = 1 + (i-1)%500000, user_id = 1 + ((i-1)%500000*7 + ((i-1)/500000)*12347) % 50000 for i in 1..2000000 (measured 2,000,000 distinct pairs; 4 likes per post). Optionally skew like the seed (per-post counts exponential around 4, 1% of posts at ~20x; the 20 newest seed posts carry 0-18 likes, mean ~4.4) so the like_count subquery for the feed's 20 posts trains on comparable fan-out. Keep ANALYZE (the seed DB has sqlite_stat1). A1: use app.rb's literal order: locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE; journal_mode=WAL; synchronous=NORMAL; foreign_keys=ON; wal_autocheckpoint=0; mmap_size=1073741824 (or 0 if v09 ships); cache_size=-65536; temp_store=MEMORY (the current trainer already has locking_mode first; keep it). New: after 'COMMIT; ANALYZE;' and the first PASSIVE checkpoint, call __gcov_reset() (declare 'extern void __gcov_reset(void);', available under -fprofile-generate) so the .gcda holds only the workload loop; or scale the loop to ~400k iterations so request paths dominate. B: in the install.sh comment for THREADSAFE=0 state the invariants it relies on: one Extralite::Database, gvl_release_threshold = -1 (extralite never releases the GVL around steps), no Database#interrupt/on_progress from other threads, checkpoint via task.async, Thread::Queue is fiber-only; any future Thread.new touching the DB is memory-unsafe. Bump the VERSION marker (e.g. "$SQLITE-pgo2") so reruns rebuild, and for local reruns delete vendor/bundle so extralite relinks against the new libsqlite3.a. Verify: 'nm /opt/sqlite/lib/libsqlite3.a | grep -c " T sqlite3_trace_v2"' = 0 and ' T sqlite3_column_decltype' = 0 as evidence the flags took effect; require "extralite" and Store.new succeed in the image; then test/test.sh 42/42 and the paired 20k bench as planned. If SQLITE_MAX_MMAP_SIZE=0 ships, PRAGMA mmap_size is silently a no-op, so app.rb and the trainer must both say mmap_size=0 (as the spec already couples them).

tech.problems:
Nothing breaks, but the variant's two halves are not equal. Measured inside tdsc-cicloid:base (aarch64 Docker, SQLite 3.54 amalgamation, gcc 13.3, the real seed/feed.db copied fresh per run, server pragmas, the load's mix and post-id choice, 100k iterations, 3 interleaved rounds pinned to one core; harness at <scratchpad>/exp/{run.sh,bench.c,sqlite_train_fid.c}).

feed_us (v01 FEED text) per round, then mean: NP no-profile 20.75/20.71/20.62=20.69; P0 shipped profile 18.87/18.80/18.94=18.87; P0r current trainer rebuilt 19.02/19.05/18.63=18.90; P1 fidelity trainer 18.15/18.40/18.38=18.31; P2 fidelity+__gcov_reset 17.87/17.88/18.08=17.94; TNP trimmed flags no-profile 24.16/20.97/23.65=22.9; TP2 trimmed flags+P2 profile 18.26/18.06/18.09=18.14. Current sorted FEED (app.rb's group_concat ORDER BY form): P0 24.13 -> P2 23.34. post_us: P0 1.12 -> P2 1.07. write_us is fsync noise (38-58) and not comparable.

(1) Part A (trainer fidelity) is real: -0.93us/feed (-4.9%) vs the shipped profile, -0.8us on the shipped sorted FEED, post -0.05us. Weighted by the load mix (46% feed, 46% post, 7% like, 1% create) that is ~0.4us of a ~50us/req paired baseline, i.e. ~0.8% end-to-end. The spec's 0.4% is conservative, not wrong. Not measured on x86_64 -march=native.

(2) Part B (SQLITE_FLAGS trim) has no measurable benefit and the spec should stop expecting one: TP2 vs P2 is +0.2us (+1%, same sign in 2 of 3 rounds, never better); TNP vs NP is +2us. Mechanism: extralite opens with SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|CREATE (no FULLMUTEX), so under THREADSAFE=2 the connection mutex is already NULL and THREADSAFE=0 only removes NULL-checked sqlite3_mutex_enter/leave calls; OMIT_DECLTYPE and OMIT_AUTHORIZATION only touch prepare time (statements are prepared once); OMIT_UTF16/OMIT_TRACE remove two well-predicted branches. It is safe, though: extralite 3.1.3's C source references none of sqlite3_trace_v2/expanded_sql/column_decltype/*16/set_authorizer/threadsafe/config (grep of ext/extralite/*.c); rebuilt against the trimmed lib: 0 undefined sqlite3_ symbols, PRAGMA compile_options = THREADSAFE=0 OMIT_AUTHORIZATION OMIT_DECLTYPE OMIT_UTF16 MAX_WORKER_THREADS=0, Database#trace (Ruby-side) still fires, Query#columns works; the real server started on it and test/test.sh passed 42/42, feed/posts/like/create curls fine. THREADSAFE=0 forces SQLITE_MAX_WORKER_THREADS=0 (PRAGMA threads returns 0); the server never sets PRAGMA threads so nothing changes. Only one OS thread ever calls SQLite (gvl_release_threshold=-1 => GVL_HOLD in common.c:253/stepwise_gvl_mode, checkpoint is an Async task, no Thread in app.rb), so THREADSAFE=0 is correct, it just buys nothing.

(3) Spec defects in Part A that must be fixed for it to deliver (the P2 numbers above are with these fixes applied): (a) the spec's pragma string lists journal_mode=WAL before locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE; EXCLUSIVE must be set before the first WAL access or the wal-index goes to a -shm file instead of heap (app.rb and the current trainer have locking_mode first). (b) 'modulo constants adjusted' naively (1+(i*7)%50000, 1+(i*13)%500000) gives only 500,000 distinct likes of 2M (lcm period 500,000); the current trainer likewise seeds only 50,000 distinct likes (period 50,000) although it loops to 200,000. train.db check: current trainer 5000 users/50,817 posts/55,714 likes, max 4 likes per post, average like_count of the top-20 feed posts 0.0 (its likes target 1+seed%50000 while new posts have ids >50000, so the like_count subquery on the feed path is trained only on empty results); fidelity trainer 50,000/500,817/2,005,715, max 16, top-20 average 3.55, vs the load's ~7.5 likes per post while it sits in the top 20 (20/0.02 cycles x 0.15/20). (c) The current trainer's run() steps every statement to SQLITE_DONE; the server does one step then reset (extralite next+reset): gcov shows sqlite3_step executed 178,984 times for the current trainer vs 98,129 for the fidelity trainer at the same 40,000 iterations, so the DONE path is trained as hot as the ROW path. (d) The current trainer sets no mmap_size/cache_size/temp_store, so getPageMMap has 0 executions in its profile (fidelity: 6.4M) while the server reads every non-WAL page through it. (e) Without __gcov_reset() the 10x seed phase is 80.6% of the profile weight (gcov line-count sum 21.69e9 vs 4.22e9 after reset; sqlite3BtreeInsert 10.2M vs 20k, walHashGet 85M), which is why P1 (18.31) trails P2 (17.94). __gcov_reset links from libgcov with -fprofile-generate, gcov.h declares it (/usr/lib/gcc/aarch64-linux-gnu/13/include/gcov.h:32), and -Werror=missing-profile still passes because the function records remain with zero counts (P2 and TP2 built).

(4) Costs: instrumented trainer run 2.1s -> 11.3-12.7s (+10s image build), train.db 12MB -> 224MB (in install.sh's mktemp dir, removed by the EXIT trap).

(5) The task's 110.4us/req baseline is stale; paired baseline runs in local-bench results are 49-55us/req. Judge this variant only with a paired A/B (same slot, interleaved), since the whole effect is ~0.4us/req.
tech.spec_fixes:
1. Keep Part A; drop Part B from this variant (or move it to its own variant with expected gain 0 and a paired A/B as the gate). If B is kept anyway, add to its spec: THREADSAFE=0 implies SQLITE_MAX_WORKER_THREADS=0 (harmless, server never sets PRAGMA threads); OMIT_TRACE is safe because extralite's Database#trace is Ruby-side; keep -DSQLITE_OMIT_DECLTYPE and -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA mutually exclusive (#error otherwise).
2. Trainer pragma string must be app.rb's order verbatim: 'PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE; PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON; PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824; PRAGMA cache_size=-65536; PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY;' (locking_mode before journal_mode, mmap/cache/temp_store present).
3. Seed: users 1..50000; posts i=1..500000 with user_id 1+i%50000 and created_at strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','2025-01-01','+'||(i*63)||' seconds') so the (created_at DESC,id DESC) index order matches id order; likes i=1..2000000 as INSERT OR IGNORE ... SELECT 1+(i*7+(i/500000)*12345)%50000, 1+(i*13)%500000 (4 distinct users per post, 2,000,000 rows; a plain (i*7)%50000 repeats every 500,000 rows). Single transaction, then ANALYZE.
4. Immediately after 'COMMIT; ANALYZE;' and before preparing the request statements call __gcov_reset() (declare via #include <gcov.h> or extern void __gcov_reset(void);). Keep -Werror=missing-profile; it passes.
5. run() = one sqlite3_step, read column 0 if SQLITE_ROW, sqlite3_reset; never step to DONE. Request loop (40,000 iterations default, argv[2] override): seed LCG; run(feed); id = max_post_id - seed%20; bind+run(post); every 7th: BEGIN IMMEDIATE, like with user 1+(seed>>8)%50000 on id, if sqlite3_changes()==0 run(exists on id), every 49th also create (body ~30 chars, author bound as ?3) and set max_post_id = sqlite3_last_insert_rowid(), COMMIT; every 1000th: run(ping) then PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE). Start max_post_id at 500000.
6. The trainer's FEED text must be the exact statement app.rb ships at that commit (v01 text only if the v01 FEED is in the stack; both the v01 and the sorted group_concat form gained from the fidelity profile, but train the one that ships). Add a comment in sqlite_train.c that FEED/POST/CREATE/LIKE/EXISTS are copies of app.rb's constants and must be kept in sync.
7. Replace the expected-gain line with: ~0.4us/req (~0.8%) from the trainer change alone, measured at the SQLite level on aarch64; verify on the x86_64 target with a paired, interleaved A/B against the current build; note the +10s instrumented build time and 224MB temporary train.db.
8. Reference implementation of 2-6 (already built, trained and benchmarked): <scratchpad>/exp/sqlite_train_fid.c (compile with -DGCOV_RESET, or make the reset unconditional when it replaces submissions/ruby-async-cicloid/sqlite_train.c).

rejected.reason: High effort and risk for an honest -5..+5% at 80k: two group-committing processes contend on BEGIN IMMEDIATE through the WAL shm (locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE must go), per-pass fixed costs double and batch sizes halve on one vCPU. The local 80k failure is a latency tail at 57% CPU, not a CPU ceiling, so doubling the fd limit is not the binding fix this phase.

Speculative busy-polling that burns the idle headroom and risks p99 at saturation; gated on an unmeasured context-switch rate; contradicted by the harness where per-request CPU already falls with load (batching), so the per-wake-up share it targets is not established. Not worth a slot.

Taken standalone it weakens the owner's documented consistency property (a read could show a row whose COMMIT later fails). v04's deferred-flush design gives readers the same no-wait behaviour while making uncommitted visibility impossible, so this id is subsumed by v04 rather than adopted as-is.

Keep-alive policy tuned to the benchmark's per-endpoint think times (close after /posts/:id and POST, never after /feed); byte-identical but it is load-test-shaped behaviour, a rule 7 gray zone the owner should decide on explicitly, not a judged variant.

Depends on two separate risky changes (dispatcher recv + direct write) plus a batch-open guard, and the README already reverted a similar inline-serving experiment (-13% saturated). Revisit only after v02/v03/v04 results exist; too many unknowns for this round.

Zero CPU gain by its own estimate; the local 80k tail (p95 ~1.06 s) is far larger than the 25-47 ms checkpoint stall, so it is not the binding latency constraint. Keep as an optional latency knob to try after v10 if p99 remains the blocker.

Measured within noise on this arm64 harness (23.29 vs 22.06 min, 23.90 vs 23.95 median) and cannot be validated here; removes stack-protector/FORTIFY/CET mitigations for an unproven 0-1%. Re-test on the x86_64 target only.

profile_summary: Baseline (ruby-async-cicloid: Ruby 4.0.7 YJIT+jemalloc, async 2.46/io-event 1.22 io_uring selector, extralite 3.1.3 on a PGO SQLite 3.54, custom HTTP/1.1 server with an FFI epoll park set and 256 worker fibers, group commit via BEGIN IMMEDIATE + per-batch Async task/Promise). In-process stackprof at 20k: SQLite ~45% (Query#next 36.6%, 92% of it the FEED statement whose plan has USE TEMP B-TREE FOR group_concat(ORDER BY); COMMIT/checkpoint/BEGIN 3.6%; LIKE insert 2.9%), io_uring kernel socket I/O ~20%, Ruby HTTP parse/serialize/write ~15% (IO#write 4.2%, HEADER regex scan 2.2%, byteindex 1.4%, String.new 1.3%), Queue hand-off + scheduler ~3%, per-batch Task/Fiber/Promise ~4-5%, GC 2.8%, JWT 3.6%; 21-22 objects/req; 1.4 syscalls/req (pwrite64 0.57, io_uring_enter 0.42 with ~7 SQEs each, epoll_pwait 0.17). Facts I verified in the image: RUBY_FIBER_SCHEDULER_VERSION is 3, and io-event's optimistic direct-syscall paths are compiled only for >= 4, so every scheduler io_read/io_write is a full SQE/CQE round trip; strace shows read_nonblock and recv_nonblock = one direct recvfrom (no fcntl, no io_uring_enter), write_nonblock and send = one direct sendto, while socket.write and syswrite go through the ring; ObjectSpace.memsize_of(socket)=288 B after read_nonblock, so the README's '4 KB rbuf per read_nonblock' concern does not apply on 4.0.7; Async::Promise#wait forwards to wait?(timeout: nil) (YJIT fallback), Thread::Queue#pop is Ruby-implemented. Harness noise: 20k us_per_req across base runs spans 55.7-110.4 (procs/slot dependent); an A/A pair was 65.5/65.7. Every variant must therefore be judged on a paired run (same slot, base and variant interleaved, ideally A/A/B) and a single-digit % claim needs at least 2 pairs. Local 80k baseline FAILS on latency, not CPU: 57.5% CPU, 69.1 us/req, p50 3.8 ms but p95 1059 ms / p99 1312 ms with 266k connects and peak_connections 65768 (above the fd ceiling) - a 1 s mode is SYN-RTO shaped (accept backlog / EMFILE sleep 0.01 at the ceiling), so churn variants are judged on 80k pass/fail and p95/p99, and the first churn run should capture nstat TcpExtListenOverflows/ListenDrops/TcpRetransSegs in the server container. Ranking logic: FEED sorter removal is the only item above 3% and is byte-identical; the socket read/write direct-syscall items and the group-commit rewrite each attack a verified structural overhead (ring round trips, per-batch Task/Promise); the micro-trim bundle is high-confidence and conflict-free; toolchain/env items are cheap to build but low-confidence locally; churn items only matter at 80k.

all_proposals.title: First read via read_nonblock into a per-worker String instead of Fiber.scheduler.io_read + IO::Buffer
all_proposals.change: http.rb `work` (lines 145-154): replace `io_buffer = IO::Buffer.new(READ_SIZE)` with `inbuf = String.new(capacity: READ_SIZE)` and pass it to `service`. `service` (lines 164-196): delete the `wait = true` flag and the `if wait ... Fiber.scheduler.io_read(socket, io_buffer, 1, 0) ... get_string ... else read_nonblock` branch; the inner loop becomes `data = socket.read_nonblock(READ_SIZE, inbuf, exception: false); break if data == :wait_readable; return disconnect(fd, socket) unless data; buffer = buffer ? buffer << data : (data.bytesize < READ_SIZE ? data : data.dup); break if data.bytesize < READ_SIZE`. After drain: `@partial[fd] = (rest.equal?(inbuf) ? rest.dup : rest) unless rest.empty?` (read_nonblock returns the outbuf itself, so a partial request that aliases inbuf must be copied before the buffer is reused; a full-size read is dup'ed for the same reason). Keep `write(socket, data) = socket.write(data)` (ring writes) exactly as is. Rewrite the comment block above `service`: a stale edge now returns :wait_readable and the worker goes idle instead of parking on a read, so MAX_WORKERS growth is no longer needed for that case (keep the constant; it is harmless). Ready-made file: scratchpad variants/http_r2.rb (generated by variants/gen2.rb from http_base.rb).
all_proposals.rationale: Under RUBY_FIBER_SCHEDULER_VERSION 3 io-event's uring selector turns every `io_read` into an SQE plus a fiber transfer to the reactor; the read of a request that is already in the socket buffer therefore costs a submit, a wait enter (when the loop is otherwise idle), a CQE decode and two fiber switches, plus `IO::Buffer#get_string` allocating the String. `read_nonblock` with an outbuf is a single recvfrom(MSG_DONTWAIT) that the scheduler does not intercept, allocates nothing, and on Ruby 4.0.7 does NOT attach a per-connection rbuf (memsize_of(sock)=288 B; RSS per connection pair 190 B with read_nonblock vs 1126 B with io_read; the README's '4 KB IO buffer per connection' concern does not hold on this Ruby). Measured: serial requests drop from 4 to 2 io_uring_enter per request; per 10k like requests io_uring_enter 641 -> 394 with 10200 recvfrom; 3-4 fewer objects per request. End-to-end probe (client on a separate CPU, server CPU-time per request, medians): mix 31.1 -> 29.75 us (-5%), feed 41.2 -> 40.5 (-2%), like 23.9 -> 24.0 (0). Second run (ab6): mix 29.6 -> ~28.3. Scaled to the 111 us Xeon baseline (per-op 1.5-2x slower) about 1.5-2 us.
all_proposals.correctness_risk: Low. Semantics preserved: EOF -> disconnect, EAGAIN -> idle (strictly better than the old 'park until the client sends' behaviour on stale edges), errors still caught by the IOError/SystemCallError rescue. Only subtlety is buffer aliasing of inbuf (handled by the two dup sites). test/test.sh 42/42 on the cumulative variant that includes this change.

all_proposals.title: Replace Thread::Queue + @waiting heuristic with an Array backlog, idle-fiber LIFO and direct scheduler block/unblock chain wake
all_proposals.change: http.rb `run` (lines 63-75): replace `@ready = Thread::Queue.new; @workers = @waiting = 0` with `@backlog = []; @idle = []; @pending = false; @workers = 0`. `dispatch` (lines 121-137): inside the Epoll.ready block replace `@ready.push(fd); add_worker if @waiting < @ready.size && @workers < MAX_WORKERS` with `@backlog.push(fd)`, and after the Epoll.ready call add `wake unless @backlog.empty?`. Add `def wake; return if @pending; if (fiber = @idle.pop) then @pending = true; Fiber.scheduler.unblock(:worker, fiber) elsif @workers < MAX_WORKERS then add_worker end; end`. `work` (lines 145-154) becomes: `inbuf = String.new(capacity: READ_SIZE); fiber = Fiber.current; loop do; fd = @backlog.shift; unless fd; @idle.push(fiber); Fiber.scheduler.block(:worker, nil); @pending = false; next; end; wake unless @backlog.empty?; service(fd, inbuf); rescue StandardError => error; Console.error(self, error); end`. Each woken worker takes one fd and wakes the next idle worker only if the backlog is non-empty, so exactly one unblock per serviced fd and no wake-ups of workers that find nothing. MUST be shipped together with proposal group-commit-yield-until-stable (app.rb), otherwise POST batching collapses (see rationale). Ready-made file: scratchpad variants/http_r3.rb.
all_proposals.rationale: Thread::Queue#pop under the scheduler goes through the queue mutex, `rb_fiber_scheduler_block`, and the `@waiting` bookkeeping on every request; dispatch's `push` unblocks a worker per fd. Micro-measured hand-off round trips: Thread::Queue push/pop 1.81 us (2 objects), scheduler block/unblock 1.61 us (2 objects), push+idle array 1.39 us. End-to-end probe on top of read_nonblock (r2 -> r3): mix 29.75 -> 28.4 us (-1.3 us, -4%), feed 40.5 -> 40.4 (0), like 24.0 -> 25.7 (+1.7). The like-mode loss has two parts: (a) with chain wake only one worker is runnable when the group-commit leader does its single `task.yield`, so batches collapse (fstat ~ commits per 10k like requests: base 207, r2 116, r3 1100); (b) with the yield-until-stable committer the leader yields once per joining member (~+2 us per POST). With the companion app change batching is restored (r3y 50 commits per 10k) and at the loadgen's ~8% POST share the net is about -1.2 us locally; feed-only traffic shows no change, so the gain is concentrated on the short GET /posts/:id and like legs. Mechanism of the full 1.3 us is only partly attributed (the micro delta is 0.2-0.4 us; the rest is the removed add_worker/@waiting heuristic and fewer spurious wake-ups), and the probe noise floor is +-1 us, hence low confidence.
all_proposals.correctness_risk: Medium. Requests on one fd stay serialised (BUSY/AGAIN state machine unchanged). Pool growth still bounded by MAX_WORKERS. Must keep `@pending` reset after block returns, otherwise a wake can be lost and backlog items sit until the next dispatch pass. Without the app.rb companion, POST bursts commit ~10x more often (durability still satisfied, but WAL write volume rises). test.sh 42/42 on the cumulative variant.
all_proposals.rule_risk: none (every response is still written only after its batch's COMMIT)

all_proposals.title: Replace the HEADER regex scan with a byteindex line walker that only byteslices the four interesting header names
all_proposals.change: http.rb `drain` (lines 243-262): replace `buffer.byteslice(line_end, head_end - line_end).scan(HEADER) do ... end` with a loop over header lines: `pos = line_end + 2; while pos < head_end; eol = buffer.byteindex(CRLF, pos); colon = buffer.byteindex(COLON, pos); if colon && colon < eol; name_end = colon; name_end -= 1 while name_end > pos && (b = buffer.getbyte(name_end - 1)) == 32 || b == 9; name_len = name_end - pos; if name_len == 14 || name_len == 17 || name_len == 10 || name_len == 13; v0 = colon + 1; v0 += 1 while v0 < eol && ((b = buffer.getbyte(v0)) == 32 || b == 9); v1 = eol; v1 -= 1 while v1 > v0 && ((b = buffer.getbyte(v1 - 1)) == 32 || b == 9); value = buffer.byteslice(v0, v1 - v0); name = buffer.byteslice(pos, name_len); case name_len when 14 then (name.casecmp?(CONTENT_LENGTH) and (return reject(socket, 400) unless DIGITS.match?(value); length = value.to_i)) when 17 then (return reject(socket, 411) if name.casecmp?(TRANSFER_ENCODING)) when 10 then (if name.casecmp?(CONNECTION) then (existing CLOSE_TOKEN / KEEP_ALIVE_TOKEN logic) end) else (authorization = value if name.casecmp?(AUTHORIZATION)) end; end; end; pos = eol + 2; end`. Add constants `COLON = ":"`, `CONTENT_LENGTH = "content-length"`, `TRANSFER_ENCODING = "transfer-encoding"`, `CONNECTION = "connection"`, `AUTHORIZATION = "authorization"`; delete HEADER and TRAILING_BLANKS. Lines without a colon are skipped (same as the regex), not rejected; the r4 variant rejects them with 400, which is stricter than today and should not be copied. Ready-made file: scratchpad variants/http_r4.rb (which has the stricter 400 to remove).
all_proposals.rationale: The regex has to be attempted at every CRLF of the head and builds a MatchData per hit; on a POST head with a ~200-byte bearer token `scan(HEADER)` costs 6.0 us and 18 objects, the byteindex walker 1.09 us and 9 objects; a GET /feed head drops from 0.385 to 0.198 us. End-to-end (r3 -> r4, 100% POST like mode) -4.4 us per request; mix -0.2..-0.9 us. At the loadgen's ~8% POST share (feed -> posts/:id -> like 15% / create 2%) that is ~0.08*4.4 + 0.92*0.2 = 0.5 us locally; the Xeon perf profile puts regex at 1.3% of CPU, which is the upper bound of this item.
all_proposals.correctness_risk: Low. Byte-level equivalent of the regex for the four headers (case-insensitive name, blanks around the colon, trailing blanks trimmed); same 400/411/413 outcomes. Keep the 'skip colon-less line' behaviour to stay byte-for-byte with test.sh; 42/42 passed on the cumulative variant.

all_proposals.title: Group-commit leader yields until no new member joined in a pass (bounded), instead of a single task.yield
all_proposals.change: app.rb `begin_batch` (lines 113-124): track members. `if @batch then @members += 1; return @batch end; @db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE"); @members = 0; batch = @batch = Async::Promise.new; Async do |task| rounds = 0; loop do seen = @members; task.yield; break if @members == seen || (rounds += 1) == 8 end; commit(batch) end; batch`. The `rounds` cap (8 passes) bounds the extra latency under a continuous POST stream; pick 4-8. Required companion of backlog-chain-wake-handoff; also useful alone. Ready-made file: scratchpad variants/app_y.rb (without the cap).
all_proposals.rationale: Today the leader yields exactly once, so only the workers that are already runnable at that moment join the batch.
